@airwavecoffee Indeed. And from any system which gives up custody of your Dogecoin and/or transfers it into other entities' wallets.

I'm pleased that many companies are building app layers or products on Dogecoin.

However, as with anything in this industry, most "investors" building "apps" just want your liquidity.

Business models often rely on more or less subtly transferring risk to ignorant users.

@Jim_HyperDoge @DogeOS This is particularly bad for Dogecoin (and holders of coins popular among retail) because retail users often do NOT understand the risks behind these "magical" yields.

Last cycle programs like this ended up in disaster for many users. I spent years warning them against it.

You do NOT need yield or false "staking" for your Dogecoin. In a way or in another you are buying into high level of risks, and you will most likely lose it all.

If you want to "stake", hold coins with staking as part of their consensus (but keep an eye on supply inflation...).

As new "investors" enters Dogecoin, they will peddle to you incredible crap.

As usual, stay away from "staking" your Dogecoin or from ANY program promising yield.

YOU WILL LOSE IT ALL.

You are buying into high levels of risk, and you do NOT need it. Stay AWAY and inform others https://t.co/ZsOacsAbBC

@Jim_HyperDoge @DogeOS Everybody should stay away from this kind of stuff - you are exposing Dogecoin folks to high level of risks with already risky assets.
